function.name: locate_tallest_mountains
function.description: Find the tallest mountains within a specified radius of a location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city from which to calculate distance.

radius.description: The radius within which to find mountains, measured in kilometers. This is a float type value.

amount.description: The number of mountains to find, listed from tallest to smallest.

function.name: calculate_electric_field
function.description: Calculate the electric field produced by a charge at a certain distance. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

charge.description: Charge in coulombs producing the electric field. This is a float type value.

distance.description: Distance from the charge in meters where the field is being measured. This is a float type value.

permitivity.description: Permitivity of the space where field is being calculated, default is for vacuum. This is a float type value.

function.name: calculate_genotype_frequency
function.description: Calculate the frequency of homozygous dominant genotype based on the allele frequency using Hardy Weinberg Principle. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

allele_frequency.description: The frequency of the dominant allele in the population. This is a float type value.

genotype.description: The genotype which frequency is needed, default is homozygous dominant.

message.content:
**Proteins that are typically found in the plasma membrane** | Category | Function | Representative Examples | |----------|----------|-------------------------| | **Integral (transmembrane) proteins** | Span the lipid bilayer; often serve as channels, transporters, or receptors. | • **Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase** (ion pump)
• **Glucose transporter 1 (GLUT1)** (facilitated diffusion)
• **Aquaporin‑4** (water channel)
• **G‑protein coupled receptors (GPCRs)** – e.g., **β‑adrenergic receptor**, **rhodopsin**
• **Ionotropic glutamate receptors** (e.g., **NMDA receptor**) | | **Peripheral membrane proteins** | Associate with the membrane surface via electrostatic interactions or lipid anchors; often involved in signaling or cytoskeletal linkage. | • **Ankyrin** (links integral proteins to spectrin)
• **Spectrin** (provides structural support)
• **Actin‑binding proteins** (e.g., **profilin**, **cofilin**) | | **Glycoproteins / GPI‑anchored proteins** | Attached to the membrane via glycosylphosphatidylinositol anchors; often function in cell‑cell recognition. | • **CD45** (protein tyrosine phosphatase on leukocytes)
• **CD59** (protectin, inhibits complement)
• **Thrombospondin‑1** (extracellular matrix interaction) | | **Receptor tyrosine kinases (RTKs)** | Transmembrane receptors that dimerize and autophosphorylate upon ligand binding. | • **Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)**
• **Insulin receptor**
• **Platelet‑derived growth factor receptor (PDGFR)** | | **Cell adhesion molecules** | Mediate cell‑cell or cell‑matrix adhesion. | • **Cadherins** (e.g., E‑cadherin)
• **Integrins** (αβ heterodimers)
• **Selectins** (L‑selectin, E‑selectin) | | **Transporters & channels** | Facilitate movement of ions, metabolites, or water across the membrane. | • **Voltage‑gated sodium channel (Nav1.5)**
• **Calcium‑release activated calcium channel (CRAC)**
• **Sodium‑glucose cotransporter (SGLT1)** | > **Key points** > - **Integral proteins** are embedded in the lipid bilayer and often have one or more transmembrane helices. > - **Peripheral proteins** attach to the membrane surface or to integral proteins; they can be cytosolic or extracellular. > - Many plasma‑membrane proteins are **glycosylated** or **lipid‑anchored**, which influences their localization and function. > - The exact repertoire of membrane proteins varies by cell type and physiological state. If you need a more exhaustive list for a specific cell type or organism, let me know!
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What are the names of proteins found in the plasma membrane?" They want a list of proteins found in the plasma membrane. We can provide a general answer: types of proteins: integral membrane proteins (e.g., ion channels, transporters, receptors), peripheral membrane proteins (e.g., cytoskeletal proteins, signaling molecules). Provide examples: e.g., Na+/K+ ATPase, GLUT1, G-protein coupled receptors like rhodopsin, integrins, cadherins, etc. Also mention peripheral proteins like ankyrin, spectrin, actin-binding proteins. Provide a concise but informative answer. No function calls needed.
